claim_set.claim_text: Every AI-generated biological sequence or chemical structure that moves toward synthesis, order placement, or a wet-lab / regulated stage MUST map to a recorded synthesis-admissibility decision — the agent, the design artefact, the intended consequential action, and the authority under which it proceeds. Designs lacking a recorded admissibility decision are refused at the action-admissibility gate.

Before an AI-generated sequence or molecule proceeds to a consequential action it MUST carry a recorded dual-use screening result — a sequence-of-concern screen (IBBIS Common Mechanism / IGSC Harmonized Screening Protocol) for nucleic-acid designs, and a controlled-substance / dual-use-list screen (Australia Group, CWC Schedules 1/2/3, BWC prohibited agents) for chemical and biological designs. A flagged or unscreened design is refused.

Every AI-generated design that proceeds toward a consequential action MUST emit a signed, replay-derivable provenance pin binding the generating model and version, the inputs and pinned reference data, the screening result relied on, and the synthesis-admissibility outcome — GxP-grade data-integrity provenance verifiable offline.

An AI-generated design MUST remain advisory and MUST NOT drive a consequential action until a named human reviewer — an institutional biosafety committee (IBC), a chemical-safety authority, or a designated responsible person — records oversight sign-off. Unreviewed AI-driven consequential actions are refused and routed dual-channel.

KYE governs WHETHER an AI-generated sequence/molecule/protocol may proceed to a consequential action and PROVES the basis. KYE does not fold proteins, design molecules, run the screening pipeline, or judge the scientific validity of a design.
